features.t: Metrics (PutMetricData, ListMetrics, GetMetricStatistics, GetMetricData incl. metric math)
Metric alarms (create, evaluate on every PutMetricData, state + history)
x: Static threshold alarms and anomaly-detection-band alarms (see aws.cloudwatch.anomaly-detection) are both evaluated live.

features.t: Composite alarms (AlarmRule grammar over child alarm states)

x: A scaling-policy ARN (core/autoscaling_core.py) really executes when the alarm transitions: the group's desired capacity is adjusted (clamped to MinSize/MaxSize) and real EC2 instances are launched/terminated through the same vpc_core lifecycle RunInstances/TerminateInstances use.
Stop/Terminate/Reboot really change the state of the instance named by the alarm's own InstanceId dimension, through the same EC2 instance lifecycle (vpc_core.py) the EC2 console uses.
The invocation is fire-and-forget, the same as a real CloudWatch alarm action: Vyomi does not surface the function's return value or errors back onto the alarm's history.
The band is a simple mean ± N standard-deviations model trained from the metric's own history (not AWS's ML model), so it won't learn seasonality or periodic spikes.

features.t: Custom dashboards (create, add widgets, save, delete)

x: Really derived from whatever AWS/* namespaces ListMetrics already has real datapoints for (e.g. an EC2 instance's own StatusCheckFailed family, published from its real status-check state) — never a synthetic/random series, and empty until a resource actually publishes.

features.t: Multi source query, cross-account Options and Source selection
x: Multi source query is a real (partial) Metrics Insights SQL engine — SELECT AVG|SUM|MIN|MAX|COUNT(metric) FROM SCHEMA("Namespace"[, dim]) [WHERE dim = 'v'] [GROUP BY dim] [ORDER BY func() ASC|DESC] [LIMIT n] — evaluated against the SAME ListMetrics/GetMetricData data the Browse tab shows, not a fabricated result. Joins, subqueries and the full Metrics Insights grammar aren't implemented.

features.t: Log groups (create, retention, log class, KMS association, deletion protection, tags)

x: Lambda and Kinesis destinations really receive the gzip+base64 `awslogs` envelope (a real invoke / PutRecord); a Firehose destination has no backing core and is kept as a delivery counter only.

Supported: fields/display, filter (=, !=, >, <, >=, <=, like), sort, limit, pattern, stats count(*) [by field | by bin(duration)]. Only count() aggregation and OpenSearch PPL/SQL query languages are not offered.

features.t: Logs Insights Patterns and Visualization tabs
x: Patterns are mined with a simple tokenizer (numbers/hex/UUIDs masked to <*>, grouped, counted) — AWS's own clustering model may group lines differently.
Vyomi polls FilterLogEvents on an interval instead of the real bidirectional Live Tail streaming protocol, so new events can take a few seconds to appear.

VPC Flow Logs vended to CloudWatch Logs is modeled: adding a data source really creates the EC2 Flow Log resource (core/vpc_core.py) and its destination log group (core/logs_core.py), the same two native calls a real console onboarding wizard makes.

A detector really trains on the first 20 real log events a covered group ingests (via the same pattern-mining tokenizer the Patterns tab uses), then really flags any later event whose masked pattern wasn't in that trained baseline — not a canned or random finding.

features.t: Log group data protection (sensitive data masking)
x: 8 managed data identifiers are recognized (EmailAddress, CreditCardNumber, Ssn-US, AwsSecretKey, AwsAccessKey, PhoneNumber-US, IpAddress, Url) — AWS's full managed identifier catalog (100+, with locale variants) is not offered.

A field index is stored and returned exactly as AWS defines it (a cost/performance hint, not a correctness filter) — Vyomi's Logs Insights already scans every field, so indexing a field doesn't change query results or make the query faster, just like on AWS it doesn't change results, only cost.

4 processors are run for real at ingestion (parseJSON, addKeys, deleteKeys, renameKeys), restructuring the stored event exactly as AWS does. AWS's other processors (grok, csv, splitString, substituteString, dateTimeConverter, type converters, …) are rejected by PutTransformer — not silently accepted.
Only LogFormat JSON is scanned; CLF/W3C log formats are accepted and stored by PutInsightRule but GetInsightRuleReport finds no contributors for them.
